title: PL/SQL Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Write a message
examples.description: An anonymous block has BEGIN and END. DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE writes a line for the client to show.

examples.title: Name a number
examples.description: DECLARE introduces local values. := assigns a value.

examples.title: Join pieces of text
examples.description: VARCHAR2 holds text. Two vertical bars join text.

examples.title: Choose an action
examples.description: IF checks a rule. END IF ends its branches.

examples.title: Choose from labels
examples.description: CASE matches a value with labels. ELSE is a fallback.

examples.title: Count with a FOR loop
examples.description: A numeric FOR loop creates a counter and includes both ends.

examples.title: Repeat while a rule is true
examples.description: WHILE checks its rule before each repetition.

examples.title: Group named fields
examples.description: A record groups related values into one local data item.

examples.title: Use a named lookup
examples.description: An associative array stores values by key. This one uses text keys.

examples.title: Return a result
examples.description: A local function gives reusable steps a name and returns a typed value.

examples.title: Handle a known error
examples.description: EXCEPTION handles a failure in the block. ZERO_DIVIDE is the name for division by zero.

examples.title: Use a fallback for NULL
examples.description: NULL means no value. NVL chooses a fallback when its first input is NULL.
